_readme: Golden question set for eval/run_eval.py and scripts/ab_chunking.py.
26 questions about the two textbooks in data/, every one anchored to a page whose
text was read and checked before the question was written (see the validator in
scripts/check_golden.py - it re-verifies the evidence is still on the cited page).
All cited pages fall inside the first 250 EXTRACTED pages of each book, so
python scripts/ab_chunking.py --max-pages 250
is a complete run - no question can miss merely because its page was not loaded.
Note the two books differ: AIMA's extracted page 1 is physical page 1, while Pattern
Classification has no text layer before physical page 13, so its extracted page 1 is
physical page 13. expected_pages are PHYSICAL page numbers, which is what the chunker
records and what _covers() compares against.
Fields per question:
question        - what to ask
expected_source - the filename in data/ the answer should come from
expected_pages  - physical page number(s); hit-rate@k checks these
reference_answer- used only by the --judge correctness score
evidence        - literal strings that must appear on the cited page; the validator
fails the entry if they do not. This is what stops a question from
quietly rotting into an unmeasurable one.
The unanswerable entries are about this project and about events after these books
were written. Neither book can answer them, so the system should decline.

questions.question: What two capabilities does a computer need in order to pass the total Turing Test?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: Computer vision, to perceive objects, and robotics, to move them about.

questions.question: For breadth-first search, is memory or execution time the bigger problem?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: Memory. Most people will wait 18 minutes for a depth-6 search, but few have the 111 megabytes it needs.
evidence: memory requirements are a bigger problem for breadth-first

questions.question: Which two search strategies does iterative deepening combine the benefits of?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: Depth-first and breadth-first: it is optimal and complete like breadth-first, but has the modest memory requirements of depth-first.
evidence: combines the benefits of depth-first and breadth-first

questions.question: In an iterative deepening search, how many times is the root node expanded?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: d + 1 times - the bottom level once, the next level twice, and so on up to the root.
evidence: root of the search tree, which is expanded d + 1 times

questions.question: What is the pathmax equation and why is it needed?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: f(n') = max(f(n), g(n') + h(n')). It ignores the misleading values a nonmonotonic heuristic produces, so f is nondecreasing along any path from the root.

questions.question: What is the Manhattan distance heuristic for the 8-puzzle, and what value does it give for the start state?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: The sum of the horizontal and vertical distances of the tiles from their goal positions, also called the city block distance. The start state gives h2 = 15.

questions.question: How is the quality of a heuristic characterized by the effective branching factor?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: The effective branching factor b* is the branching factor a uniform tree of the same depth would need to contain the number of nodes the search generated.

questions.question: What kind of problem was simulated annealing first used extensively to solve?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: VLSI layout problems, in the early 1980s. It has since been applied to factory scheduling and other large-scale optimization tasks.
evidence: VLSI layout problems in the early 1980s

questions.question: Does alpha-beta pruning change the move that minimax would return?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: No. Applied to a standard minimax tree it returns the same move, pruning only branches that cannot influence the final decision.
evidence: returns the same move as minimax

questions.question: How many custom VLSI chips will Deep Blue use, and what search depth will that allow?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: A parallel array of 1024 custom VLSI chips, roughly one billion positions per second, reaching depth 14.

questions.question: What is the scoring in the wumpus world - the reward for the gold and the penalty for dying?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: 1000 points for climbing out of the cave carrying the gold, a 1-point penalty per action, and a 10,000-point penalty for getting killed.

questions.question: What is the ontological commitment of propositional logic compared with first-order logic?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: Propositional logic commits only to facts; first-order logic commits to facts, objects and relations.

questions.question: What form does a Horn sentence take, and why does that class matter?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: P1 AND P2 AND ... AND Pn => Q, where the Pi and Q are nonnegated atoms. It is the class for which a polynomial-time inference procedure exists.

questions.question: What replaces MINIMAX-VALUE in games that include an element of chance?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: EXPECTIMINIMAX-VALUE, which computes expectimax and expectimin values at the chance nodes.

questions.question: What are effect axioms in the situation calculus?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: Axioms describing an action by stating the properties of the situation that results from doing it - for example, that grabbing a present portable object leaves the agent holding it.

questions.question: Who pointed out the frame problem as a major problem for the use of logic in AI?
questions.expected_source: Artificial Intelligence - A Modern Approach - Russel, Peter And Norvig, Stuart (Ebook - English).pdf
questions.reference_answer: McCarthy and Hayes, in 1969.

questions.question: In minimum-error-rate classification, why is the decision generally determined by the more likely state of nature?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: Because the loss incurred for an error is greater than for being correct, so both loss differences are positive - though the posteriors must still be scaled by those differences.
evidence: loss incurred for making an error is greater

questions.question: What does knowledge of the covariance matrix let you calculate about the data?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: The dispersion of the data in any direction or in any subspace; for y = A'x the density is N(A'mu, A'SigmaA).
evidence: dispersion of the data in any direction

questions.question: In Case 3, where each category has an arbitrary covariance matrix, what shape are the discriminant functions and the decision surfaces?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: The discriminant functions are inherently quadratic and the decision surfaces are hyperquadrics - hyperplanes, hyperspheres, hyperellipsoids, hyperparaboloids and so on.

questions.question: In signal detection theory, what are the four probabilities relating the internal signal to the threshold called?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: A hit, a false alarm, a miss, and a correct rejection.

questions.question: How is the maximum likelihood estimate of a parameter defined?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: The value of theta that maximizes p(D|theta) - the value that best agrees with the observed training samples.

questions.question: Give an example of a trivial sufficient statistic and say why it is of little interest.
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: A vector whose components are the n samples themselves. Such statistics are of little interest because they provide no real summary of the data.

questions.question: What are the two methods of choosing the region for density estimation, and which one grows the volume until it encloses k neighbours?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: Shrinking the region as a function of n, which is the Parzen-window method, and specifying kn as a function of n such as kn = sqrt(n), which is the kn-nearest-neighbor method - that is the one that grows the volume until it encloses kn neighbours.

questions.question: What partitioning of the input space does the nearest-neighbor algorithm produce?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: A Voronoi tesselation: cells of all points closer to one training point than to any other, each labelled by that point's category.

questions.question: In a Bayesian belief network, what do the links between nodes represent?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: Conditional probabilities - for example P(c|a), described by a matrix of entries P(ci|aj).
evidence: links between nodes represent conditional probabilities

questions.question: What model parameters does hidden Markov model learning determine?
questions.expected_source: Pattern Classification by Richard O. Duda, David G. Stork, Peter E.Hart .pdf
questions.reference_answer: The transition probabilities aij and bjk, estimated from an ensemble of training samples.

unanswerable.question: What does the Pinecone Starter plan cost per month?
How do I set CHROMA_COLLECTION in this project's .env file?
Which company released GPT-4 and in what year?
